html:
On 8 December 1962 armed followers of the Brunei People's Party rose against the sultan and the British, seeking a state of North Borneo. British and Gurkha troops from Singapore crushed the revolt within days.

The party had just won every elected seat in the legislature, and opposed joining the planned Malaysia. Rebels seized police stations and the Seria oil field.

The sultan suspended the constitution and ruled by emergency decree, which is still renewed today. In 1963 he decided not to join Malaysia. The revolt also gave Indonesia's Sukarno a cause for the Konfrontasi.
